survivor_audit.reasoning: My V21 (drop the BootstrapResult grading) also survives. The two principal guards are mutually redundant. My V17 removed the OUTER replayOwner guard (the one MG9's reason leans on) and the suite still caught it as INV-REPLAY-FOREIGN-PRINCIPAL-REFUSED via the inner guard; the receipt's MG16 shows the opposite direction. Both-off is caught, so the property is collectively asserted - the disclosed reason is true.

My V19 disabled the fallback and the run stayed PASS 154. bootstrapReplay always reads the live binding row, which already carries project_id because the bind and the replay record commit in the same transaction, so the assignment is unreachable. Correctly labelled a no-op mutation rather than a missing assertion.

My V33 removed that single assignment and stayed PASS; the same branch increments skippedSubtrees, which is in the same absence gate. The gate itself is load-bearing (V29 and the executor's T4 fail four ids).
Same redundancy in the link branch; the link property is asserted by INV-NO-ENTRY-CROSSES-A-JUNCTION, which my V38/V39 kill.

True for the predicate: my V37 (predicate returns true for this card's own selector) fails ROUTE-TRUTH-TABLE. Not true for the wiring: my V36 (routeLegacy ignores the predicate and always forwards) keeps the bare program at PASS with a foreign id set - no assertion inside the check sees it. It is caught only by comparing the emitted ids against the expected set, which the dispatched parity rows and this review do, not by the 154. The receipt should say 'caught by the dispatched rows', not 'superseded'.

My V05 survives. Every writer (bindProject, RevokeWorkspaceBinding, nextRevision) derives the revision from the row it just read inside the same transaction, and store.Open serialises on a single connection, so no legal public sequence presents the stale value. Correctly disclosed as a backstop; it becomes load-bearing the moment a pooled connection or a second writer exists, which is exactly when the migration-owned table in the parent-gate obligation should add a store-level constraint.

My V03 survives. On Windows a slash-only string is not volume-qualified and contains no backslash, so it falls through to the minted-id lookup and is refused as NOT_FOUND instead of FORBIDDEN. Same denial, different class - which the receipt states. Worth one assertion feeding a slash-only ref so the typed refusal is pinned.

But 'no reachable input' overstates it - the suite already proves it can inject a hostile adapter for the scanner (badScanner, scopedScanner), and the same trick with a hostile WorkspaceAuthority would reach this guard. Disclose it as 'no fixture exists' rather than 'no input exists'.

The missing-root sibling IS asserted (V25 kills INV-MISSING-ROOT-REASON-CLASSIFIED). reservation_or_block_reason: REJECT on W04-01-EVIDENCE alone; no product blocker, no recovery blocker, no scope violation. What is good and should be said plainly: the implementation is sound (24 of my 41 mutations died on named assertions, including every security and honesty obligation the earlier rounds forced), the round-2 recovery blocker is genuinely closed (I ran the real CreateBackup/RestoreBackup and the poisoned-row control myself), registry parity is complete across all 13 selectors I exercised, all 26 recorded artifact hashes verify, the three rejections are disclosed honestly rather than narrated away, and the domain_objects storage placement is acceptable as interim. This is NOT a cosmetics rejection either: a receipt that states 'the surviving-mutation list is complete' when five further reachable branches survive, that carries the same three-versus-four gofmt contradiction round 3 named as a rejection ground, that publishes a required_evidence_ids pair no artifact supports, and that binds a 152-assertion check report to a 154-assertion headline does not satisfy the card's own evidence requirement, which explicitly asks for the not-passed items. To clear this card a resubmission must, inside the existing write scope: (1) regenerate check_report.json from the delivered run and refresh regression_log.txt's binding row to the invocation the receipt cites, or relabel both as historical captures; (2) fix the four count errors - three-versus-four gofmt files, addendum repeats one not two, 29+12+3+1 equals 45, 25 not 27 probes for round 3; (3) either record the id-to-requirement mapping behind required_evidence_ids or delete the field; (4) complete the surviving list with V02, V07, V09, V23 and V24/V26 and restate U4/U5 as 'no fixture exists' rather than 'no reachable input'; (5) record the non-passing rows: W12-C13 at 1 COMMAND_FAILED per 3 attempts with the harness's own 8 ids, and W04-C01, W06-G02 and task-only W06/W12/W17 as COMMAND_FAILED on both routes; (6) add four assertions to tests/context/check (a slash-only ref on the read path, the recorded measurement mode being FIXTURE, the stage row's file_failures after a partial import, and one typed refusal asserted by its Fault code), which also closes the two genuine coverage gaps this review found. None of it requires reopening the product code.
